---

## Role Assignment

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**For data collection, decide:**

- Who will be **experimenter** for each session?
- Who will be **assistant** (handling materials)?
- Who will **recruit participants**?
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Rotation plan:**

Everyone should run at least one session as experimenter to understand the process.
:::
::::

## Quick Procedure Rehearsal

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your groups (5 minutes):**

1. One person reads through the procedure aloud
2. Others check against the written version
3. Clarify any last questions about timing or wording
:::

---

## Participant Recruitment

::: {.callout-tip}
## Who Can Participate?

Today you can recruit:

- Other students in the lab (from different groups)
- Rotate so everyone gets to be both experimenter AND participant
- Ensure no one participates in the same study twice

**Cross-test**: Group A tests Group B, Group B tests Group A, etc.
:::

---

::: {.poll-box}
**Instructor Check:**

Before data collection begins:

- All materials ready?

- Procedure rehearsed?
- Recording sheets prepared?
:::

# Data Collection {background-color="#275882"}

## Live Testing (~75 min)

---

## Data Collection Ground Rules

::: {.definition-box}
**During data collection:**

1. Follow your procedure EXACTLY as written
2. Use standardised instructions (read from script)
3. Do not improvise or add explanations
4. Record data immediately and accurately
5. Complete debriefing after EVERY participant
:::

---

## Being a Good Experimenter

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Do:**

- Be professional and friendly
- Speak clearly at consistent pace
- Allow time for questions
- Stay neutral (no hints!)
- Thank every participant
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Don't:**

- Rush through instructions
- React to participant responses
- Skip the debriefing
- Forget to record data
- Change wording between participants
:::
::::

---

## Handling Problems

| Situation | What to Do |
|-----------|------------|
| Participant has question about task | Repeat standardised instructions only |
| Technical problem | Note it, try to resolve, record the issue |
| Participant wants to withdraw | Thank them, destroy their data |
| Data looks unusual | Record it accurately, note concerns |
| Procedure takes too long | Complete it, adjust timing for next participant |

---

## Data Recording Best Practices

::: {.callout-important}
## Record Accurately

- Write clearly and legibly
- Use participant numbers (not names)
- Record everything (even mistakes)
- Note any unusual circumstances
- Double-check entries before participant leaves
:::

---

## Activity: Begin Data Collection

::: {.exercise-box}
**Data collection rotation (~75 minutes):**

1. Groups pair up to exchange participants
2. Run your study with multiple participants
3. Aim for **at least 5 participants** per group in this session
4. Rotate experimenter roles within your group
5. Record ALL data and any issues that arise

**Instructor will circulate to observe and support!**
:::

---

## During Data Collection

::: {.callout-note}
## Instructor Observation Focus

As you circulate, note:

- Are procedures being followed consistently?
- Are instructions being read verbatim?
- Is data being recorded properly?
- Are participants being debriefed?
- Any ethical concerns?
:::

---

# Data Quality Check {background-color="#275882"}

## Reviewing Your Data (~15 min)

---

## Data Quality Checks

::: {.definition-box}
**After collection, verify:**

1. All data sheets are complete (no missing entries)
2. Participant numbers are consistent
3. Condition assignments are recorded correctly
4. Any unusual data points are noted
5. All participants were debriefed
:::

---

## Activity: Review Your Data

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your groups (10 minutes):**

1. Collect all data sheets from this session
2. Count total participants tested
3. Check for any missing data
4. Note any participants to exclude and why
5. Calculate remaining participants needed
:::

---

## Data Collection Progress

::: {.poll-box}
**Quick tally around the room:**

- How many participants did each group test today?
- How many more do you need for your target N?
- Any groups with data collection problems?
:::

---

## Common Data Issues

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Missing data | Note pattern; may need to exclude participant |
| Impossible values | Check recording; verify with participant if possible |
| Condition confusion | Review allocation method |
| Too few participants | Plan additional recruitment |
| Inconsistent administration | Retrain experimenters, check procedure |
